transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Another boy from the valley. You all come the same way. The well swallows names and reasons alike, so keep yours if you can.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I cannot keep my name to myself because I am Salim and my brother Omar was taken by this place. I jumped in to get him back, and I will not leave without him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Another oath spoken into stone. The well took a boy already, and it has no care for brothers or promises.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He is my brother, and I promised my mother I would watch him. Please, you must have seen him pass this way.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I have seen many pass, their faces blur like smoke on rock. The well keeps what it takes, and it does not answer pleas.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: But he's just a child, and it was my fault he fell. You have to tell me where the pale hand took him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Fault is a stone everyone carries down here. They sent you alone for him, not even a torch to lie with you in the dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: They didn't send me, I jumped because I had to save him! Please, tell me where the tunnels go.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Had to. That word echoes loud in caves like this. Tunnels go where the King wills, not where a brother points.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What King? I don't care about kings, I just need to find the pale hand that took him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You say that now. Down here, all paths bend toward the King of Jinn, whether you care or not.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then tell me how to get to this King if he has my brother. I will walk any path to find Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Every boy says he will walk any path, until the stone asks its price. Your feet are soft with the valley still, and the King hears such vows as noise.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have already lost everything if I don't get him back. I don't care what else this well takes from me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: So you say, before it eats your memories one by one. Many swore they had nothing left, yet they screamed loudest when the well began to choose.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It can eat whatever it wants from me as long as I find Omar first. Just point me where the King is so I can beg for my brother back.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Begging is a language the King does not learn. He sits where the rock glows dimmer, and even knees wear thin before him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's not just a demand, it's my fault he's here! You have to help me, Hanash, I know that's your name.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: …How do you carry that name down here. They remember me? Or do they remember the story they told about me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The elders in the village still whisper about Hanash who vanished years ago. They say you were lost to the darkness, but you are real, and you are here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Whispers grow when a man cannot answer them. Tell me, boy, do they say I was foolish — or that I was abandoned.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: They say you were foolish to play near the edge, just a story to scare us children. I was the foolish one who sent Omar there, not him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: So the village chose an easy lie. It is lighter to call a man foolish than to say no one came for him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Nobody came for you, and I am sorry you were left alone in the dark. I cannot let Omar be abandoned like that.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I waited. For years I watched the mouth of the well, thinking a rope might remember me even if the people did not.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I didn't wait for a rope, I jumped straight in because I couldn't leave him. Please help me so Omar doesn't have to wait in the dark like you.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Come closer, Salim, and carry this like a coal, not a weapon. Say this before you face the King: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. Do not say it twice — the well listens for the second time faster than the first. There is one more. It costs me more than the first did.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Give it to me. I am ready.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I will carry them all the way to him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when your mind begins to slip. Use the second only when the hands reach for you — not before. The order matters.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will not forget. And I will not forget you either, Hanash.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Go then, before the square decides it has heard enough. May you find a better end than mine.
